findings.rule: As in c00600: every store to mem[64] is a constant >= 96 or the old value plus a non-wrapping amount, so mem[64] >= 96 and writes at mem[64] + c (c >= 0, below 2^64) never alias slot 64; then 'x = mem[64]; mem[x + k] = ...; mem[mem[64]] = x - mem[64] + n' folds to mem[x] = n, the sha3/call/revert buffers resolve as for constant bases, and 'x - mem[64]' with x = mem[64] and no store to 64 in between is 0.

notes: Very long functions reviewed by structure (calls, branches, reverts, returns, loops): estimateSwapIn (11615-13114) and estimateSwapOut (13115-14644) with their core (routing, sqrt, price-limit) read in full; getDexLimits (1230-2048) read in full; getPoolReserves, getPoolReservesAdjusted, getPoolsReserves(Adjusted), getAllPoolsReserves(Adjusted) (1350-1620 lines each) by structure: they are the same inlined code (getPoolTokens, try this.getDexPricesAndExchangePrices, the reserves getters, getDexLimits). Semantics checked and found right: swapIn/swapOut try/catch with ADDRESS_DEAD (57005), _decodeLowLevelUint1x, the No-pools branch, the signed routing formula and its check order (legacy right-operand-first), price formulas, _priceMoveExceedsLimit both arms, reserve normalisation, limits. Implicit loops: 6 return-encoding loops (375, 1060, 4920, 6544, 9787, 11571) and 2 string-decoding copies of VERSION()'s result (13099, 14625) are P7; the 5 'while idx - 1' allocation loops of new Pool[] / PoolWithReserves[] print their first iteration before the loop (P3); 2 address[] calldata decoders are fine. P12: each getDexLimits copy duplicates the tail of the token0/token1 borrowable block in both arms of 'maxBorrowLimit > borrow' (1909-1937 vs 1941-1969, 1975-2008 vs 2012-2045; 18 such arms in 9 copies). P11: 45 'if -block.timestamp + A + B > SafeMath.add(A, B): revert' under 'if block.timestamp <= SafeMath.add(A, B)', and 9 Panic(50) checks implied by the loop bound. P8: ~2300 zero-initialisation lines of memory structs, most dead, plus 23 back-to-back mem[64] stores. P18: 262 'require mem[a] == mem[a + 12 len 20]' address checks and 42 'Bytes(12, 0), mem[..]' on returned structs. P9: the two FixedPointMathLib.sqrt expansions per estimate function (lines of ~3000 characters) and products distributed over differences ((expandsTo - withdrawable) * expandDuration printed as mem[288] * ED - ED * W).
summary: Semantically faithful as far as read (all branches, reverts, calls and returns of the source are present), but the text is dominated by memory noise: free-pointer-relative buffers left raw (155 P2 lines, hidden revert reason and hash input), ~2300 zero-initialisation lines, duplicated tails, expanded sqrt, and values re-substituted instead of named.
